Sensitive antennae gently wave, feeling the eddies and flow of air for disturbances. When the diminutive lanceleth begin to sense the 
rhythm of larger creatures, they spring into action, leaping forward in an explosion of darting slugs. With unerring accuracy they spear 
through flesh and chitin alike, and dig into feast. Alone they can be a painful pest, but when they swarm during the warmer seasons, 
they can often take down prey much larger than their size would suggest, as each successful hit spurs on more to strike in kind. As their 
prey stumbles from blood loss and the pain of squirming bodies of slugs in their open wounds, nearby scavengers are drawn to the 
scent and cries, closing in the vulnerable beast to fi nish it off.

Encountering Often found on the coast shallows, within sunken 
caves, marshlands and drowned woods, drawing out a lanceleth 
swarm is as simple as it is dangerous. Disturbing the water 
or making any general ruckus can often trigger a single slug 
to launch itself. Within moments the rest of the swarm soon 
follows and it is advisable for a Traveler to hide behind a shield 
or barricade before too late.
